data.narrative:
SiPearl, a Series A semiconductor company founded by Philippe Notton, has raised €130M to date. Valuation is assessed against a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor players (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage peers in chips and semiconductors, including SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the €130M raised as a proxy for current value, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding €260M ($260M). Peer-median valuation across 3 same-stage, same-sector comparables produces a $2.3B implied value; the peer range spans $2.0B (d-Matrix) to $11.0B (SambaNova). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, a standard limitation for private companies. The public semiconductor sector trades at a 18.4x median price-to-sales multiple.

The two applicable methods yield a triangulated range of $221M (low), $1.3B (median), and $2.7B (high). The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around SiPearl's competitive positioning and commercialization trajectory relative to its peer set. The peer-median approach carries significant weight given direct comparability, though the outlier SambaNova valuation ($11.0B) suggests stage and sector multiples remain volatile. Revenue realization and product differentiation remain critical valuation drivers.
